title: Logarithmic differentiation of x^x and beyond
solution:
(i) **Power rule:**
$$\frac{d}{dx}x^{a}=ax^{a-1}.$$

(ii) **Exponential rule:** using $a^{x}=e^{x\ln a}$,
$$\frac{d}{dx}a^{x}=a^{x}\ln a.$$

(iii) **Logarithmic differentiation.** Write $x^{x}=e^{x\ln x}$. Then
$$\frac{d}{dx}x^{x}=e^{x\ln x}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(x\ln x)=x^{x}\left(\ln x+1\right).$$

(iv) Let $y=x^{(x^{x})}$. Taking logarithms,
$$\ln y=x^{x}\ln x.$$
Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$ (using (iii) for $\frac{d}{dx}x^{x}$):
$$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{x}(\ln x+1)\ln x+x^{x}\cdot\frac{1}{x}=x^{x}\left[(\ln x+1)\ln x+\frac1x\right].$$
Therefore
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{(x^{x})}\cdot x^{x}\left[(\ln x+1)\ln x+\frac1x\right].$$

(v) Simplify first: $(x^{x})^{x}=x^{x\cdot x}=x^{x^2}$. Using logarithmic differentiation on $x^{x^2}=e^{x^2\ln x}$:
$$\frac{d}{dx}x^{x^2}=x^{x^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(x^2\ln x)=x^{x^2}\left(2x\ln x+x\right).$$

So the answers are:
$$\text{(i) }ax^{a-1},\quad\text{(ii) }a^{x}\ln a,\quad\text{(iii) }x^{x}(\ln x+1),$$
$$\text{(iv) }x^{(x^{x})}x^{x}\left[(\ln x+1)\ln x+\tfrac1x\right],\quad\text{(v) }x^{x^2}(2x\ln x+x).$$
hints: For x^x, write x^x = e^(x ln x) and use the chain rule.
For x^(x^x), take logs and use the result from (iii).
